ut_junkie_boulders.blurb: A quiet cluster of boulders in Little Cottonwood Canyon, tucked among trees near the Hidden Forest boulders and reached from the canyon trail. It is all bouldering, with 14 problems that run from an easy V1 warm-up up to a V10. The middle of the range is where most of it sits: half the problems are V4, with a handful of hard V7 to V9 lines above. Some of the lines are on tall boulders beside the main trail, and a bit of bushwhacking may be needed to reach others. Expect little company, and bring a couple of pads since landings can be uneven.

ut_road_kill_wall.blurb: A short sport wall in the lower part of Maple Canyon, a brief hike up-canyon beyond the Schoolroom area. The 14 routes are all bolted conglomerate sport lines, with one also set up as a top rope. The grades sit on the friendly side: a few 5.5 to 5.6 leads for newer climbers, a cluster of 5.7 and 5.8 routes at the heart of the wall, and just a few 5.9 to 5.10 lines for those wanting more. Climbs are fairly short, around 35 feet, which makes this a good spot for building confidence or for groups with mixed ability.

ut_narcolepsy_area.blurb: A steep, smooth quartzite cliff in Big Cottonwood Canyon, just beyond the JHCOB Wall and partly hidden behind pines. It is shady and cool, so it suits warm days. The 14 routes are mostly trad lines (12), plus a couple of sport routes, and range from 5.7 up to 5.11, with the bulk at 5.9 and 5.10. Some of the climbs have anchors, so top-roping and lead options both exist. The approach starts where Stairs Gulch meets the road and gains height steeply, so expect a workout before you rope up.

ut_watchtower_tiers.blurb: Two terraces of rock set directly above the main Watchtower wall in Ferguson Canyon, on the Wasatch front. The lower tier has an older, more traditional feel, while the upper one is newer and more heavily bolted. Of the 14 routes, 10 are sport and 4 are trad, though cracks run through the cliff so some lines can be protected either way. Difficulty starts around 5.9 and climbs to 5.12, with most routes at 5.11 and 5.12: this is a place for climbers who already lead the harder grades, though a couple of easier routes serve as warm-ups.

ut_richfield_bouldering.blurb: A scattering of boulders on the hillside above the west edge of Richfield, right beside I-70 in central Utah, which makes it an easy break on a long drive. There are 14 problems spread over several small groups of boulders, such as Gate Boulder and Romance Boulder. The difficulty is gentle: mostly V1 to V3, a couple of V4s, and a single V6, so it works for beginners and casual sessions. It sees plenty of sun, though shade is usually possible to find.

ut_pack_rat_boulder.blurb: A bouldering spot in the Sentinel Area of Moe's Valley, on the edge of St. George in southwest Utah. The 14 problems are on conglomerate, graded from V0 up to V6, and most fall in the V3 to V5 band, which makes it a decent stop for intermediate boulderers. Several lines are sit starts. Problems here include The Conqueror at V5. It sits alongside Duality in the same section of the valley, so the two are easily combined in one session.

ut_duality.blurb: A bouldering area in the Sentinel Area of Moe's Valley, near St. George in southwest Utah. It holds 14 conglomerate problems with a wide spread: easy V0 and V1 lines, a middle group around V4 to V6, and a few serious hard problems reaching V9 and V10. Duality itself is the namesake boulder here. Reached on foot from the valley's main parking, it works best outside the hot months, since the rock heats up in summer and shade is limited.
